gate: No construction gameplay implementation until the combined 20 ideas, then 200 additional ideas, are fully specified and cross-deduplicated; 220 total.

concepts.title: Joinery Loom — six-mode tactile placement
concepts.novelty_audit: Existing game only draws static farmhouse primitives and has no construction or multi-mode snapping; this unifies snap/freeform/blueprint under one reversible action model rather than six incompatible editors.
concepts.player_scenario: Player selects a timber post, drags its translucent ghost near a wall anchor, holds a precision modifier to nudge 5 cm, switches to freeform when a socket is unsuitable, and commits or cancels without losing materials.
player_loop: Pick a part from inventory; choose socket, magnetic, grid, freeform, guided blueprint or continuous paint; inspect ghost validity and cost; confirm atomic placement; undo if needed.
simulation_rules: Canonical world transform quantized to 0.01m and yaw to 1 degree for saved commands; preview never consumes inventory; only committed server-authoritative local action reserves resources; typed sockets take precedence in socket mode; no placement through occupied solid volumes; freeform still obeys collision and support rules; undo must restore previous transform and exact resource counts.
service_contracts: ConstructionPlacementService: proposal/validation/commit/rollback only; InputAdapter maps all devices into intent verbs; InventoryService owns debit; StructureGraph owns anchors; GameSave owns persistence.

controls.mouse_keyboard: Left-click pick/confirm, right-click cancel, wheel rotate, Shift precision, Tab cycle mode, Ctrl+Z undo.
controls.gamepad: Left stick moves ghost on plane, right stick rotates, shoulder cycles mode, A confirms, B cancels, D-pad nudges.
controls.touch: Tap select, drag ghost, two-finger rotate, visible precision/snap toggles, confirm/cancel buttons; never rely on long-press alone.

original_asset_plan: Original procedural beams, translucent ghost material, socket glyphs
haptic/audio feedback from self-authored samples, color-independent valid/invalid icons.

performance_budget.desktop: At most 1 active ghost, 64 nearby sockets queried, 1ms CPU preview budget at 60fps target.
performance_budget.mobile: At most 1 ghost, 24 nearby sockets queried, 2ms CPU preview budget at 30fps target; no per-frame mesh regeneration.

godot_acceptance: Given 2 wood and valid post anchor, preview costs 2 but inventory unchanged until confirm; confirm places exactly one post and deducts 2 wood.
Repeat the identical command ID twice and assert exactly one post and one debit.
Replay placement, cancel, undo, save/load and verify identical world transforms and inventory.
adversarial_tests: Zero wood, occupied anchor, unsupported freeform, invalid mode, NaN transform and rapid double confirm must reject without mutation.
Undo a load-bearing post with dependents must reject or cascade only after explicit consent; no silent orphan geometry.
concepts.engine_portability: Portable canonical placement commands, numeric transforms, typed socket graph and validation reasons; Godot uses Node3D/RayCast3D adapters, Unreal/Unity adapters consume same serialized commands; physics parity must be retested.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Full refund on canceled preview; exact debit reversal on valid undo; never duplicate consumed material.

concepts.title: Groundweave — sculpt-to-foundation terrain kit
concepts.novelty_audit: Current flat valley terrain and farmhouse lack terrain-aware building. The novelty is a player-editable support lattice that suggests terracing, stilts or retaining edges based on sampled slope and erosion exposure.
concepts.player_scenario: Player outlines a hillside cabin footprint, previews three alternative foundations and their costs, adjusts supports by dragging handles, and watches rain channels change before committing.
player_loop: Draw footprint; sample heights and soil; compare pad/terrace/pier alternatives; adjust supports and drainage; reserve stone/wood; build terrain-safe supports; inspect rain resilience.
simulation_rules: Sample footprint at 0.5m intervals, deterministic triangulation order; no support with negative embed depth; enforce 2m path clearance, lake/field exclusion and slope caps; terrace operations must not modify farmland without explicit authorization; terrain change and support construction are a single undoable transaction.
service_contracts: TerrainQuery read-only height/slope/soil; FarmOccupancy read-only plot protection; StructureGraph receives supports; Inventory owns stone/wood; SaveService stores geometry and revision.

controls.mouse_keyboard: Draw polygon by click, drag handles, scroll styles, Enter commit, Esc cancel.
controls.gamepad: Move cursor with left stick, A place vertex, X style, shoulder handle selection, B undo vertex.
controls.touch: Tap footprint corners, drag supports, bottom style selector, large commit and back controls.

original_asset_plan: Original mossy retaining blocks, wood pier variants
ground contour decals, rainwater flow arrows and support-pressure indicators.

performance_budget.desktop: <=128 footprint samples and 40 support nodes in preview, <=3ms CPU on desktop.
performance_budget.mobile: <=64 samples and 20 supports, <=5ms CPU on mobile; precompute erosion only when edited.

godot_acceptance: Sloped 6x8m footprint produces pad, pier and terrace quotes with distinct valid support graphs.
Committing a pier foundation changes no protected farm bed and persists identical heights/supports after reload.
Changing weather from clear to rain updates erosion risk without silently changing built structure.
adversarial_tests: Reject footprint intersecting lake, zero-area polygon, duplicate vertices, invalid heights, stale terrain revision and unavailable materials.
Undo must restore exact terrain revision and original soil cells even after cancel.
concepts.engine_portability: Store support graph and footprint in engine-neutral meters; Godot TerrainQuery may initially use flat-plane stub but must mark slope simulation unverified; future Unreal landscape/Unity terrain adapters are not drop-in.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Quoted quantities reserved atomically; demolition salvage based on actual intact supports.

concepts.title: Framewright — inspectable house assembly timeline
concepts.novelty_audit: Existing farmhouse is one static mesh cluster. Here every structural phase is an interactive, inspectable construction step with dependencies, partial occupancy and NPC help.
concepts.player_scenario: Player raises foundation posts, braces a frame, sets walls and roof, opens a door, then decorates; unfinished buildings remain visible and safe through multiple seasons.
player_loop: Plan structure; place foundation; erect beams; add braces and walls; roof; weatherproof openings; furnish; each stage yields playable visual and gameplay consequences.
simulation_rules: Stage graph FOUNDATION->FRAME->SHELL->WEATHERTIGHT->HABITABLE; missing required braces block heavy roof; each part has stable ID and prerequisite anchors; no automatic instant house completion; weather exposure affects unfinished materials; player can pause and resume without reset.
service_contracts: StructureGraph authoritative part IDs and load edges; VillageJob can supply optional labor; FarmInventory supplies resources; WorldRenderer shows stages; Principal Save owns serialized lifecycle.

controls.mouse_keyboard: Hover part and click place; R rotate; Tab stage timeline; E inspect joints.
controls.gamepad: Radial build palette, D-pad phase selection, A place, Y inspect, B back.
controls.touch: Bottom step cards, tap highlighted joint, pinch camera, dedicated undo and inspect.

original_asset_plan: Original beam joinery, framing joints, roof shingles
worksite signage, cloth tarps and stage-specific construction sounds.

performance_budget.desktop: <=300 structural nodes and 600 render instances per small home; mesh batching target <3ms render submission.
performance_budget.mobile: <=150 nodes visible, merged static geometry at settled stages; LOD and low-poly framing.

godot_acceptance: Building cannot become habitable before supported roof, doorway and weatherproof shell are complete.
Save after frame-only stage and reload exact part graph, resources and active construction stage.
Apply roof before bracing and receive actionable missing-brace reason.
adversarial_tests: Reject cycles in part dependency graph, nonexistent parent, negative work ticks, part duplicate ID and zero-resource completion.
Interrupted save mid-build must restore last committed stage and not auto-finish.
concepts.engine_portability: Serializable stage DAG and material transactions independent of Godot; Godot Node3D visual hierarchy is derived from part graph; Unreal/Unity need separate mesh and animation adapters.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Costs charged per completed step; unfinished plan has zero material charge; each part ledger tracks actual paid units.

concepts.title: Rainroof Atelier — weather-reactive roof craft
concepts.novelty_audit: Beyond decorative roof variants, players engineer roof slope, overhang, gutter and rainbarrel paths that measurably alter crop water availability and house weather exposure.
concepts.player_scenario: Player tests two roof pitches in a rainstorm, installs a gutter to a barrel, then uses harvested rain to irrigate a greenhouse.
player_loop: Shape roof geometry; preview drainage arrows; route gutter sockets; attach cistern; see daily rainfall capture; use stored water in farm irrigation.
simulation_rules: Only sealed roof planes collect water; captured volume bounded by rainfall*projected_area*efficiency; water not created from clear weather; overflow routed to ground; disconnected gutter yields zero cistern capture; winter freeze reduces flow and may damage unprotected fittings.
service_contracts: RoofGraph owns geometry; HydrologyService (Farming F02) supplies rainfall ledger; InventoryService owns gutters/cisterns; FarmWater adapter consumes transferred water; calendar day_epoch prevents duplicate harvest.

controls.mouse_keyboard: Drag roof ridge/eaves, wheel pitch, click socket route, H view water arrows.
controls.gamepad: Shoulder roof plane, left stick adjust pitch, A attach, X toggle rain overlay.
controls.touch: Drag ridge handles, pitch slider, tap source/target sockets, toggle rainfall overlay.

original_asset_plan: Original ceramic tiles, straw thatch, rain chains
animated droplet decals, water gauges, moss accumulation and soft rain audio.

performance_budget.desktop: Roof graph <=100 planes, water flow once per day; preview under 2ms CPU.
performance_budget.mobile: Roof graph <=40 planes, simplified flow arrows; no per-frame fluid physics.

godot_acceptance: Given 10mm rain, sealed 20m² roof and 80% efficiency, capture equals 160 liters before gutter/cistern limits.
Disconnected gutter stores zero water and overflow does not disappear from accounting.
Year rollover and save/load do not grant rainfall twice for same day_epoch.
adversarial_tests: Reject negative rain, zero-area polygons, reverse-flow cycle, over-capacity cistern, and a second collect action on same epoch.
Clear-weather and snow/frozen cases must not create liquid water.
concepts.engine_portability: Water ledger uses fixed integer milliliters and plane areas; renderer adapters for Godot/Unreal/Unity differ but water conservation and graph are portable.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Water is transferred, never minted; materials charged for each physical gutter/barrel.

concepts.title: Roomheart — spatial rooms that remember life
concepts.novelty_audit: Current village relationship scores are disconnected from houses. This creates recognized rooms with functional purpose, privacy, warmth and residents' learned preferences.
concepts.player_scenario: Player partitions a loft into a kitchen and cozy bedroom; a villager moves into the bedroom after an invited household event and adjusts their schedule and comfort.
player_loop: Build enclosure; assign room function based on fixtures; furnish; evaluate light/warmth/space; invite consenting NPC; observe changed home routine and dialogue.
simulation_rules: A room must be closed polygon with navigable door, minimum area and roof coverage; comfort combines light, shelter, heating and preference weights, clamped 0..100; room use cannot overwrite NPC consent or existing housing; no occupied resident can be removed by deleting room without relocation workflow.
service_contracts: StructureGraph room detector; VillageLife resident schedule/consent authority; Weather/Heating read-only comfort input; SaveService persists assignments; HUD shows room feedback.

controls.mouse_keyboard: Click enclosure, choose function from room panel, drag furnishings, inspect comfort bars.
controls.gamepad: Focus room by D-pad, radial function selector, A assign, Y inspect resident needs.
controls.touch: Tap enclosed floor, room function cards, large resident consent dialogue buttons.

original_asset_plan: Original interior wallpapers, cozy lamps, curtain variants
furniture kits, warmth/light overlays and localized room labels.

performance_budget.desktop: Room detection event-driven; <=50 rooms/house; <=2ms rebuild when wall topology changes.
performance_budget.mobile: <=20 rooms/house; no continuous comfort recomputation; recompute at day/weather changes.

godot_acceptance: Two enclosed rooms with door connectivity produce separate room IDs and correct comfort changes.
A consented NPC moves to a valid bedroom and schedule changes persist through save/load.
Deleting occupied bedroom requires explicit relocation and never deletes NPC identity.
adversarial_tests: Reject room with no door, nonmanifold boundary, zero area, unreachable entrance, non-consenting NPC and duplicate room assignment.
Annual time progression must not forget household membership.
concepts.engine_portability: Portable polygon room and resident assignment model; Godot NavigationServer3D, Unreal NavMesh and Unity NavMesh require parity tests.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Fixtures have explicit inventories and cannot be counted in two rooms; moving room boundaries preserves item ownership.

concepts.title: Hearth Threads — visible household utility weaving
concepts.novelty_audit: Unlike static lamps, players connect fictionalized, nontechnical utility tokens to room sockets, routing heat, light and water through an inspectable network with capacity and seasonal demand.
concepts.player_scenario: Player runs a magical warmth-thread from a hearth to a bedroom, sees cold spots fade, then reroutes it around a blocked doorway.
player_loop: Place a source; connect colored thread sockets; assign priority; inspect room warmth/light/water; resolve broken links by rerouting.
simulation_rules: This is explicitly fictional game logic, not real-world electrical or plumbing instructions; graph nodes have integer capacity units, directed edges and losses; output cannot exceed source generation; cycles resolved deterministically or rejected; failed connection never debits materials; disconnected rooms revert to ambient comfort.
service_contracts: StructureGraph supplies typed sockets; Roomheart consumes delivered heat/light; Weather supplies demand; Inventory owns materials; no physical-world hazardous engineering specifications.

controls.mouse_keyboard: Click source then destination socket, drag route around obstacles, press U for capacity overlay.
controls.gamepad: Select source with A, steer routed ghost with stick, A attach, X cycle utility type.
controls.touch: Tap two endpoints, draw safe fictional route, visible color-independent capacity indicators.

original_asset_plan: Original glowing fiber ribbons, hearth runes, water sigils
warm bloom particles, low-motion alternatives and capacity icons.

performance_budget.desktop: <=150 graph nodes and 300 edges per settlement; solve on graph edits or hourly simulation ticks.
performance_budget.mobile: <=60 nodes and 120 edges per active area; precomputed simple glow, no particle-heavy route simulation.

godot_acceptance: A 10-unit source with 2-unit loss delivers at most 8 units to its sink.
A disconnected bedroom loses supplied warmth and shows a clear reason.
Save/load and yearly replay do not create stored utility units.
adversarial_tests: Reject negative capacities, nonexistent endpoints, duplicate edge IDs, cycle exploits, overflow, invalid type sockets and broken source nodes.
Disconnect/undo restores resource ledger exactly without energy duplication.
concepts.engine_portability: Graph solver and integer accounting portable; Godot uses MultiMesh ribbons and room shader effects, Unreal/Unity use native rendering adapters.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Utility tokens consumed on physical node creation; thread relocation charges only incremental length with deterministic refunds.

concepts.title: Memory Blueprints — replayable house patterns
concepts.novelty_audit: Instead of opaque instant prefab placement, a blueprint stores a semantic construction graph, lets players compare affordable build stages, and adapts to local terrain without cloning paid resources.
concepts.player_scenario: Player saves a custom cottage blueprint, carries it to a new valley plot, previews foundation substitutions and asks neighbors to help assemble its stages.
player_loop: Capture built part graph; normalize origin and stable sockets; version template; place ghost on new plot; resolve terrain and budget; schedule staged assembly.
simulation_rules: Blueprints are plans not item containers; no items copied when saving a blueprint; instance IDs freshly generated; template graph canonical ordering; substitutions require explicit approval; invalid version/schema rejected; user-authored exports contain no protected external meshes or assets.
service_contracts: StructureGraph supplies parts; TerrainQuery validates adaptation; Inventory owns resource debits; ConstructionStage service tracks progress; SaveService owns blueprint revisions.

controls.mouse_keyboard: B opens blueprint library, click capture, drag plan ghost, mousewheel rotate, click stage commit.
controls.gamepad: Radial blueprint library, left stick move, shoulder rotate, A confirm plan, X view cost.
controls.touch: Template cards with preview, drag-and-rotate ghost, prominent cost and cancel buttons.

original_asset_plan: Original parchment-blueprint UI, line-art 3D hologram
material icons, construction stamps and compact thumbnail renders.

performance_budget.desktop: <=500 template parts, preview instancing under 5ms when moved; cache normalized graph.
performance_budget.mobile: <=200 visible template parts, LOD silhouette preview, no per-frame topology rebuild.

godot_acceptance: Capture and instantiate a 20-part blueprint; plan consumes zero wood until construction stage advances.
Adapting to sloped ground generates explicit foundation substitutions and updated cost.
Save/reload blueprint revision and plan without duplicated parts or missing ownership.
adversarial_tests: Reject cyclic template, malicious external resource path, negative bill, invalid schema and conflicting site occupancy.
Cancel a partially paid plan returns only unspent reservations and does not refund completed consumed work.
concepts.engine_portability: Engine-neutral graph JSON, transform units and license references; renderer/physics and asset paths remapped by future Unreal/Unity importers.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Capturing/placing a plan is free; executing each physical step consumes validated inventory.

concepts.title: Village Build Commons — community construction economy
concepts.novelty_audit: Existing Village paid shifts do not alter structures. This introduces transparent, NPC-scheduled cooperative construction where each helper has availability, skill, wages and social consequences.
concepts.player_scenario: Player posts a village bridge repair, donates lumber, hires two neighbors for weekend shifts, and sees scaffolding and a repaired crossing appear as milestones finish.
player_loop: Choose civic project; publish budget; solicit NPC help; deliver materials; schedule work; observe staged site progress; celebrate or mediate setbacks.
simulation_rules: NPC participation requires availability and relationship/contract agreement; labor hours capped per day_epoch; pay only for completed work; no duplicate donation reward; progress advances by scheduled work and weather constraints; cancellation refunds unspent materials but not paid labor; no coercive social penalties for declining.
service_contracts: VillageLife owns NPC consent/schedule, FarmEconomy owns wages and material ledger, ConstructionStage owns milestone graph, WorldPathing owns bridge navigation, SaveService owns records.

controls.mouse_keyboard: Open notice board, click project and resources, calendar drag shifts, inspect scaffold hotspots.
controls.gamepad: Notice-board cards, D-pad select shift, A assign, Y inspect costs.
controls.touch: Large notice-board timeline cards, drag worker portrait to day slot, confirm payments.

original_asset_plan: Original village notice board, modular scaffolds, workwear
tool animations, construction dust, celebratory banners and localized dialogues.

performance_budget.desktop: <=20 concurrent civic sites, 12 workers/site, event-driven progress; <=1ms simulation tick.
performance_budget.mobile: <=5 active visible sites, simplified worker animations, shared meshes and no real-time crowd physics.

godot_acceptance: Two workers with 4-hour shifts advance exactly 8 worker-hours and receive exactly 8 hours of agreed pay.
Declining NPC or unavailable schedule causes no debit or reputation penalty.
Bridge repair changes traversal path only after structural milestone acceptance and persists after reload.
adversarial_tests: Reject duplicate shift IDs, overlapping worker shifts, negative wages, donation double-submit and unavailable materials.
Cancel/restart must not mint resources or leave orphaned navigation connections.
concepts.engine_portability: Serializable civic project graph and schedules portable; Godot uses navigation region adapters, Unreal/Unity require platform-specific path rebuild and animation retargeting.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Donation receipts keyed by donor+transaction ID; wages charged once per fulfilled shift; unspent donation refunds on cancellation.

concepts.title: Salvage Ledger — reversible renovation with provenance
concepts.novelty_audit: Construction undo usually ignores downstream dependencies. This system previews safe detach order, material wear and recoverable salvage, so renovations become a strategic loop instead of infinite refunds.
concepts.player_scenario: Player remodels an old barn: removes a roof after supporting beams, salvages weathered planks, repairs them, and rebuilds a greenhouse without duplicating stock.
player_loop: Inspect structure; plan safe disassembly; add temporary braces; remove parts in dependency order; recover quality-rated materials; refurbish or trade; reconstruct.
simulation_rules: Detach only leaf parts or after validated support substitution; salvage return <= original paid units minus wear/loss; salvage quality 0..100; repeated demolition ID is idempotent; any refund requires actual part removal; temporary braces cost resources and are returned only when removed; restore must not produce duplicate part IDs.
service_contracts: StructureGraph computes dependencies; Inventory owns salvage and repairs; WeatherWear service computes quality; SaveService persists receipts; ConstructionStage tracks partial buildings.

controls.mouse_keyboard: Click part with dismantle tool, see dependency highlights, Shift add brace, Enter confirm.
controls.gamepad: Radial renovate mode, A inspect, X brace, Y salvage preview, A confirm.
controls.touch: Tap component, step-by-step safe removal cards, hold-to-confirm demolition with alternate accessible button.

original_asset_plan: Original worn wood/stone texture tiers, highlighted load paths
scaffold props, repair bench and salvage sorting visuals.

performance_budget.desktop: Graph traversal O(parts+edges) per selected part, <=400 part home; no per-frame topology scan.
performance_budget.mobile: <=160 active parts, incremental dependency cache and low-resolution wear variants.

godot_acceptance: Removing a 4-wood beam at 25% loss yields at most 3 wood-equivalent salvage and removes beam exactly once.
Attempting to detach sole roof support returns explicit blocking dependencies.
Save, load and replay same demolition transaction does not award salvage again.
adversarial_tests: Reject repeat transaction ID, salvage above paid amount, detached parent with dependents, negative wear, stale graph revision and interrupted repair.
Undo of salvage already spent must fail with an actionable debt/repair plan, not silently duplicate materials.
concepts.engine_portability: Provenance and deterministic salvage arithmetic independent of engine; geometry and particles require Godot/Unreal/Unity adapters.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Conservation law: recovered<=paid, each part removed once, quality loss explicit, material spent on repair never generated freely.

concepts.title: Seasonwright Homes — structures that respond to climate
concepts.novelty_audit: Current valley has seasonal weather but homes are inert. This adds visible aging, seasonal shelter choices, recoverable maintenance and habitat benefits without punishing cozy play.
concepts.player_scenario: Player reinforces a cottage before winter, adds a shaded veranda for summer, and chooses a green roof that attracts pollinators while raising upkeep.
player_loop: Observe seasonal exposure; select upgrades; preview shelter/pollinator/crop effects and costs; install; see weather-dependent visual and NPC comfort feedback.
simulation_rules: Wear per day bounded 0..100 and computed from weather+material+protection once per day_epoch; no instant catastrophic collapse; each upgrade has explicit tradeoff; player gets warnings and recovery paths; pollinator benefit bounded by habitat distance; decorative appearance cannot silently alter farm output without approved farm adapter.
service_contracts: Weather/Calendar supplies monotonic epoch; StructureGraph owns upgrades; VillageLife reads shelter/comfort; FarmPollination adapter receives bounded modifier; SaveService stores wear and epoch.

controls.mouse_keyboard: Click house seasonal overlay, compare ghost upgrades, Enter install, R repair.
controls.gamepad: Open home status, D-pad season tab, A inspect/upgrade, Y compare.
controls.touch: Season cards, clear before/after diagrams, accessible repair controls with no tiny handles.

original_asset_plan: Original seasonal wall patinas, snow caps, vine growth
green roofs, shutters, pergolas and subtle weather VFX with reduced-motion options.

performance_budget.desktop: Once-per-day per-building wear; <=200 structures per region, cached overlays and no continuous degradation loops.
performance_budget.mobile: <=50 visible structures, baked material variants, no dynamic snow accumulation geometry.

godot_acceptance: Same building in winter with/without insulation shows bounded shelter differences and deterministic wear.
Two calls in same day_epoch cannot double-charge wear or farm bonus.
Save at Winter day 14 and reload Spring year+1 retains upgrades, condition and correct epoch.
adversarial_tests: Reject invalid upgrade dependency, duplicate epoch processing, negative wear, unlicensed art dependency and missing farm modifier adapter.
When pollinator system absent, upgrade remains cosmetic/comfort-only and no invented yield gain is claimed.
concepts.engine_portability: Portable weather-driven wear rules, structural upgrades and habitat modifiers; renderer and material systems require Godot/Unreal/Unity separate implementations.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Upgrades charge exact quoted items; repairs consume material and cannot generate positive net resources.
